audit.title: Tokenized Asset Data Streams

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The implied question — "which tokenized asset streams exist and what are their IDs?" — is answered only by a `Loading...` placeholder. No liftable chunk contains an actual stream. The intro sentence is a redirect, not an answer.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean hierarchy — 1 H1, H2 max depth, 0 level skips (per facts). But sections are near-empty (median 12 words) and the two data regions ("Streams Verifier Network Addresses", "Mainnet Tokenized Asset Streams") render nothing static. Good skeleton, no meat.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Facts confirm 0 numerals, 0 units, 0 hex identifiers. For a page whose purpose is publishing stream IDs and contract addresses, this is the core failure — all specifics are behind JS.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 5 internal links to related canonical hubs (discovery endpoint, LINK token contracts, supported networks). Reasonable internal linking; zero external/primary-source links, though for a listing page that's acceptable.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No sentence defines "tokenized asset data stream." An engine cannot lift a definition of the page's own subject.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Valid JSON-LD (both blocks parse), canonical set, full og/twitter coverage. Weakened by auto-generated artifacts: `datePublished` == `dateModified` (never-revised/generator-stamped), keywords are tokenized fragments ("and", "ID."), and all four `about` entries use the "Content about X" template — low-value entity signals.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks. For a reference listing this is partly expected, but no copy-pasteable verification snippet or example stream-ID usage is shown.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Title matches "tokenized asset data streams" queries, but "what is the stream ID for [asset]" and "verifier address for [network]" — the actual dev queries — resolve to nothing retrievable. No troubleshooting or FAQ.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: The little prose present is clear and consistently named. Nothing to fix here beyond volume.

audit.summary: This is a reference/listing page whose entire payload — the tokenized asset stream IDs, network names, and verifier addresses — is client-side rendered and reaches a crawler only as `Loading...`. As served, the page contains 55 words, zero numerals, zero hex identifiers, and no table, so a generative engine sees a title and three navigation links but *none of the data the page exists to provide*. The single biggest opportunity is not prose polish: it is making the stream inventory present in server-rendered HTML so it can be retrieved and quoted at all. Metadata scaffolding (valid `TechArticle` + `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD, canonical URL) is the one genuine strength; everything downstream of retrieval is starved because the body is empty.

recommendations.title: Server-render the stream inventory
recommendations.where: "Mainnet Tokenized Asset Streams" and "Streams Verifier Network Addresses" sections.
recommendations.issue: `Loading...` — the data table is client-side only.
recommendations.change: Emit the stream table (asset name, stream ID, network, verifier proxy address) in static HTML, or provide a server-rendered fallback. Numbers, hex stream IDs, and addresses must exist in the served DOM.
recommendations.why: Engines and agents cannot retrieve or cite content they never receive; this is the difference between an invisible page and a citable one. Highest-lift change on the page.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first lead sentence with the canonical definition
recommendations.where: Directly under the H1, before the tutorial link.
recommendations.issue: Page opens with "To learn how to use Data Streams, see…" — a redirect, not an answer.
recommendations.change: Lead with a self-contained sentence, e.g. "Tokenized Asset Data Streams are Chainlink Data Streams that deliver [NAV/price] data for tokenized real-world assets; each stream is identified by a unique stream ID and verified onchain via a network-specific verifier proxy. The table below lists all available streams and their IDs."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim-liftable definition and frames the table as the answer to the page's implied query.

recommendations.title: Render the table as a real HTML `<table>` with headers
recommendations.issue: Facts show 0 tables; data (once rendered) risks being an unstructured widget.
recommendations.change: Use a semantic table with columns (Asset, Stream ID, Network, Verifier Proxy Address). One row = one coherent retrievable unit.
recommendations.why: Comparison/lookup tables are high-extractability structures engines parse cleanly for justified answers.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/lookup-phrased sub-headings
recommendations.issue: Headings are concept-titled ("Mainnet Tokenized Asset Streams") not query-shaped.
recommendations.change: Add anchors/subheads like "How do I find a tokenized asset stream ID?" and "Verifier proxy addresses by network," matching how devs query.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept titles miss.

recommendations.title: Fix metadata template artifacts
recommendations.issue: keywords include "and"/"ID."; `about` entries all read "Content about X"; `datePublished` == `dateModified`.
recommendations.change: Replace keyword fragments with real entities (e.g. "Chainlink Data Streams", "tokenized assets", "verifier proxy"); give `about` meaningful descriptions; stamp `dateModified` from actual revision time.
recommendations.why: Cleaner entity signals and a genuine freshness date raise E-E-A-T and entity resolution. (Lower priority — schema cannot help a page whose body is unretrievable.)

recommendations.title: Add a minimal usage snippet linking ID → verification
recommendations.issue: No code showing how a stream ID is consumed.
recommendations.change: Add a short, tagged snippet (e.g. Go/Solidity) passing a stream ID to the verifier, with imports.
recommendations.why: Gives agents a concrete, copy-pasteable path from listing to action.

antiPatterns: **Empty/placeholder content:** Core data renders as `Loading...` — a wall of nothing, not a wall of prose, but equally unretrievable.
**Auto-generated keyword/entity noise:** keyword list includes stopword "and" and fragment "ID."; `about` entries are template placeholders.
offPageNotes: Consider `llms.txt` and ensuring the stream inventory is exposed via the discovery API endpoint (already linked) as an agent-friendly structured source.
Client-side rendering is a site-level architecture decision; if the table must stay dynamic, publish a server-rendered or static JSON/CSV mirror that crawlers and agents can ingest.
